description: zero_one_bfs independent finite and metamorphic tests
state: Deterministic finite fixture executions and assertion verdict vectors for the adjacent implementation; not an all-input proof.
cost: Finite enumeration 3^9 graphs at 3 sources, simple-path oracle factorial in vertex count in general but n=3 here; other fixtures linear in 2048. Symbolic suite cost, no timing claim.
forward: Six tests: enumerate all 3^9 directed three-vertex graphs, each of three sources, and compare against recursive enumeration of simple paths; then assert global ordered errors, stale improvements/zero cycles/parallel edges, vertex relabeling and duplication, a 2048-vertex chain plus isolated vertex, and a nonunique distance fiber.
inverse: In the universe of fixture/verdict pairs, excluded behavior contains a passing verdict when any encoded expected value differs, or a claim of universal correctness from these finite fixtures. The independent oracle enumerates paths rather than reproducing the production scheduling mechanism.

Given the all-pass assertion vector, recover all candidate implementations agreeing with the fixture map on exactly the executed inputs. This set includes the reference and implementations that fail on untested inputs; it does not identify unique source code. A failing oracle assertion constrains the preimage to implementations disagreeing on that concrete graph/source/output.

Simple paths suffice because all weights are nonnegative: deleting a cycle never raises cost. Enumeration covers 19,683 graph codes and 59,049 graph/source comparisons including self loops. Oracle seen-state prevents cyclic recursion.

Replacing the production checked edge increment by zero must disagree on a reachable unit-weight edge; the exhaustive oracle assertion rejects this compiled mutation. An initial reversed-comparison mutant allowed positive-cycle growth and was manually stopped, so it is not counted as an assertion witness.

Fixtures sample graph semantics, source/endpoint priority, disconnected behavior and metamorphic identities. They do not exercise allocation failure or the defensive checked-distance overflow return. Repeatability means identical normalized named test outcomes across two debug and two release runs, not identical timings.
checks: cargo test -p mova-algorithms --offline --lib (debug and release, twice each)
Strict all-target Clippy, rustfmt check, two identical syntax projections, compiled production mutant assertion rejection.
limitations: Finite observations are not a universal proof; syntax projection is partial.
Defensive arithmetic overflow branch is not exercised; no executable approximate profile attached.
